mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production (INDPRO) curve signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered late-cycle episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of at least 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered labor-softening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months, accompanied by a concurrent drop in housing starts (HOUST), indicates broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and depresses earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered supply-contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 3% year-over-year while the federal funds rate remains below 1%, it signals a delayed monetary policy response to inflation, which erodes real corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from a neutral benchmark (t-test p > 0.05) during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) coupled with a flat or declining personal income (implied from GDPC1/PAYEMS ratio) signals a precautionary savings regime, reducing consumer spending and thus corporate revenue, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered precautionary-saving episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >50,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered labor-expansion episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% over three months, without a corresponding drop in unemployment, signals a housing-specific demand shock that reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equities, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered housing-demand-shock episodes.
